question.text: Nikhil's adviser recommends Strategic Asset Allocation (SAA) while his friend Gaurav's adviser uses Tactical Asset Allocation (TAA). Which statement CORRECTLY distinguishes between the two approaches?

answer.text: SAA involves frequent portfolio changes based on market views, while TAA maintains fixed long-term weights
SAA and TAA are identical approaches with different names used by different regulatory bodies
SAA focuses on "timing the markets" while TAA focuses on "time in the market"
SAA sets long-term target weights emphasizing "time in the market," while TAA makes short-term deviations to exploit opportunities, emphasizing "timing the markets"

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series X-A pages 263-264, Strategic Asset Allocation (SAA) is the long-term target policy portfolio allocation based on the investor's characteristics and objectives — the philosophy is "time in the market." Tactical Asset Allocation (TAA) is a short-term decision taken within the SAA framework to exploit market opportunities — the philosophy is "timing the markets." The Trap: Option A reverses the definitions completely — a classic exam trick. Option C also reverses the mnemonic. These reversal traps catch candidates who have superficial familiarity with the terms. Note: SAA sets the long-term policy mix; TAA is a short-term overlay within SAA to capture perceived opportunities.
